title: Red tide hits Carigara Bay; shellfish ban stays in 2 Samar bays

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — The Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) has warned the public against the gathering, selling, and eating of shellfish from Carigara Bay in Leyte after seawater samples tested positive for a red tide-causing organism, while a shellfish ban remains in effect in two other bays in Samar and Eastern Samar. In its latest advisory issued on Monday, BFAR-8 said seawater samples from Carigara Bay, which covers the coastal municipalities of Babatngon, San Miguel, Capoocan, Barugo and Carigara, tested positive for Pyrodinium bahamense, an organism associated with paralytic shellfish poisoning.
